newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends higher on Colombia strike news.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends higher on Colombia strike news.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended sharply higher on Tuesday, bolstered by local and speculative buying amid news that a truckers' strike in Colombia slowed the country's coffee exports, traders said.

Spot September arabicas jumped 6.90 cents per lb on the day, to 187.10 cents, after ranging from 188.00 to 183.00 cents. Active December ended 4.20 cents higher, at 167.15 cents, while the back months closed up 3.00 cents.
"It was mostly locals and mostly on the Colombia truckers' strike," said Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast. "There is the idea that the strike might spread and cut off the shipment of coffee."
A truckers' leader in Colombia said on Tuesday that the strike by truck drivers in Colombia's main Pacific coast port of Buenaventura had blocked the export of about 21,000 60-kg bags of coffee.

About 60 percent of Colombia's coffee exports are shipped out of Buenaventura. The strike began late Saturday but passed virtually unnoticed, given that it came during a three-day bank holiday weekend.

"No trucks are going in or out of the port. We have about 3,000 trucks immobilized in and around Buenaventura and about 30 of them are loaded with about 700 bags each of coffee," Javier Suarez, head of the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association ACC told Reuters.
The ACC declared the strike to protest transport companies' failure to increase freight rates in line with an accord hammered out at the end of a strike in April.
Suarez said the ACC, which represents about 85 percent of the country's truckers, could extend its action to Colombia's Atlantic coast ports if there is no agreement in the next 24 hours.
Colombia is the world's second largest producer of coffee after Brazil.
While the Colombian strike fueled some speculative interest, traders continued to note that falling open interest and thin volume exaggerated price movement.

Total open interest as of August 18 stood at 19,523 lots, down 523 lots from the previous session. Open interest in September, which goes into delivery period on Thursday, stood at a still relatively high 4,568 lots.
After Tuesday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks rose by 355 60-kg bags as of August 18, to 92,783 bags -- or the equivalent of about 371 lots.
However, an additional 23,625 bags of coffee were pending grading, the exchange said.
Some traders said the build up in coffee stocks awaiting grading could weigh on the market, although they noted a large amount of coffee put up grading against July failed to pass board approval.
Volume on the day reached an estimated 5,228 lots.
